notes.urn:cts:latinLit:tmp1342.tmp1342.opp-lat: Prologue: 'a me pontificali apice proferendo' is obscure; rendered literally. The sentence about the acts sent to Ceraunius is elliptical; a verb such as 'sent' is supplied. In §6 'nobilissimam nobilitate familiam, quam coepistis' lacks a verb; 'complete' is supplied. 'mater' in §6 apparently refers to Leonilla, their grandmother. Stray letters (footnote marks a, b, c etc.) omitted; 'pe(??)' read as 'per', 'pasionem' as 'passionem', 'eui' as 'cui'.

The text here reads Palmatius throughout; the glossary's 'Palmasius' should be corrected to Palmatius. In §9 'pa(??)i(??)er' is damaged, read as pariter ('together'); 'obumbrabit' taken as obumbravit. In §10 'infra' is taken as 'inter se' (among themselves). In §14 'propter meritum eorum qui advenerant' is obscure; rendered 'on account of the regard of those who had gathered' — possibly 'metum' (fear of the crowd, cf. §17) is meant.

Stray footnote letters (a, b, c, d) omitted. In 16, 'putaremur' read as 'putarentur'. In 17, 'sauciorum' (of the wounded) may be an error for 'sanctorum'; translated as printed. 'Tantum originale purgavit peccatum' is odd; rendered literally ('purged only original sin'). In 18, 'c de ideramus' read as 'desideramus'; 'appropinquassem' read as 'appropinquassent'. In 19, 'vix maximae' read as 'viae maximae'. In 20, 'esi' read as 'est'. In 21, 'noti' is unclear, possibly corrupt for 'non' or 'notarius'; left untranslated. Urbatus is presumably Saint-Geosmes near Langres.

nodes.text: THE ACTS OF THE TRIPLET MARTYRS SAINTS SPEUSIPPUS, ELEUSIPPUS [AND] MELEUSIPPUS, BY SAINT WARNAHAR, PRIEST OF LANGRES.
(From the Bollandists, Acta Sanctorum, January, vol. II.)
THE AUTHOR'S PROLOGUE.

1. To the holy lord Pope Ceraunius, who is to be set by me at the pontifical summit, Warnahar [sends] greeting. You never cease to be made equal in merits to the foremost persons of the most blessed bishops, and in every conduct of your priesthood you hasten daily to be adorned with holy religion; by the study of reading the divine writings you have travelled through all doctrines; now, devout, you intend to gather in the city of Paris the acts of the holy martyrs, for the love of religion and to the heaping up of your praise. Hence you are to be made equal to the holy Eusebius of Caesarea in zeal of emulation, and to be remembered for ever with a like gift of glory. Pardon our lack of skill, since we are not able to praise you as much as you would deserve to be preferred in [our] heart, if eloquence came to our aid. The acts of the holy twins, who in the suburb of the city of Langres gained the precious consummation of martyrdom, and [those] of the most blessed Desiderius, martyr and bishop of that same city, as you commanded with devoted zeal, so you may know [them sent] by me most eagerly in the obedience of service.
CHAPTER ONE.
The coming of Saint Benignus to Langres.

2. We are compelled, with Christ as author, to reveal more zealously the glorious contests of the martyrs, which we confess beyond doubt were carried out in love of faith in him. Therefore it is fitting, by the fullest reason, to explain rather than to pass over with what great rewards the three holy twin brothers Speusippus, Eleusippus and Meleusippus came to the dignity of martyrdom. It is truly to be marvelled at, and to be extolled in many ways [as] by the predestination of almighty God. So, following the order of this matter, and weighing more carefully the benefits of the Giver of graces, let us make known the beginning.

3. Now, holy Polycarp, bishop of the city of Ephesus, perfectly instructed in the teaching of the most blessed John, apostle and evangelist, filled with the Holy Spirit, desiring under the leadership of faith to enlarge the army of Christ, was sending his disciples through the various parts of the world to preach boldly to the nations the word of our Lord Jesus Christ. So, hearing that the emperor Aurelian, after the departure of Severus the impious persecutor, had once more stirred up a most cruel persecution, and that a worse prince had succeeded a bad prince in the realm, and that he had promulgated an edict before himself and his governors to the provinces of the Gauls and generally to all the people subject to him, and had decreed that all Christians whatever should be punished with various torments, blessed Polycarp sent there, for the sake of preaching, holy priests of God, namely Andochius and Benignus, priests, and Thyrsus, a deacon: men most outstanding in virtues, poured out in the love of God, eager for the struggle of the contest, wholly devoted to taking on the toils of journeys for the name of Christ, not slow to endure the dangers of the sea, glad to seek pilgrimages eagerly and to leave their parents gladly for the religion of Christ, desiring rather than fearing the torments of punishment or the passion of a blessed death.

4. These three men, obedient to the holy admonitions, boarded a small ship, and the holy Polycarp, bidding farewell to the holy men, gave them this charge: 'Go, brave men, fighting bravely in the bravery of Christ; through the holy confession of Christ gain many fellow-soldiers, with whom, triumphing in victory, you may obtain a name and the everlasting glory of dignity. May the fruits of your labour be heaped up with manifold wealth; may the seats of the righteous in paradise rejoice greatly through you in the gaining of holy souls.' With these and many other prayers holy Polycarp escorted them.

5. They, sailing successfully under divine guidance, quickly reached the shores of Marseille; and having gone ashore, with an angel of God going before them, making a prosperous journey, they entered the city of Autun; and there, by the Lord's providence, they found Faustus, a man of most noble family, distinguished by senatorial rank and raised to the praetorian fasces, and were most gladly received by him as guests. When he learned that they were priests, he humbly asked that they make his friends and household Christians through the washing of baptism. For he, because of the impending persecution, was worshipping Christ in secret. He also presented his son, the youth Symphorian, who through the preaching of the saints and by divine predestination was in later times to be a renowned martyr. And handing him into the holy hands, he earnestly besought that he be baptized by holy Benignus and received from the sacred bath of the font by holy Andochius. They, eagerly carrying out the work for which they had come, and complying with the prayers of so great a man, satisfied the desires of his will in all things through the grace of baptism.

6. After this, when the aforesaid Faustus had examined more carefully the purpose of their request through conversation with the holy priests, divine goodness brought his sister and her grandsons to his memory. Then he said to them: 'I have a full sister, Leonilla by name, a noble matron, a citizen of the city of Langres; she has, from a son, three grandsons, twin brothers born together at one birth, educated in the liberal arts, yet still living by their father's tradition in pagan error; their [grand]mother desires to join them to the army of Christ. Come to the aid of her devotion, most holy priests, and [complete] in its nobility the most noble family which you have begun.' When this was said, the holy men, considering more carefully the matter for which they had come, agreed on the plan that holy Benignus should hasten to enlighten the territory of Langres, according to God's will. But Saints Andochius and Thyrsus, greatly increasing the town of Autun through divine preaching, not long afterwards were crowned with a happy martyrdom under the emperor Aurelian. So the aforesaid Faustus sent holy Benignus at once to his sister as a divine gift, which he was. She received him with all veneration, like the manna that came down from heaven.
CHAPTER II.
The triplets are invited to the faith by their grandmother's admonition and by dreams.

7. On that same day her said grandsons were offering profane sacrifices with the customary rite at the image of the goddess Nemesis in a field called Palmasius, and they had kept back for their grandmother the remains of the superstitious offerings; inviting her to the feast, they brought out what they had kept. But she, throwing it all to the dogs, spurned it like dung. Then, approaching them from a distance with holy Benignus, she began to speak such words: 'Dearest grandsons, know that our Lord Jesus Christ is true God, to whom angels and every creature render due service, who established the whole world and composed all the matter of things, balanced, by the sudden ordering of his word; with the same vision he stretched out the height of heaven; he spread wide and wider the manifold expanses of the lands; by a momentary decree he ordered the immense sea of the deep to be gathered and confined by shores; he painted the sky with stars, and establishing two chief lights, he wholly decreed that they should adorn in successive alternation all that he had made, and, clothed in light, reveal all things; he granted the whole sea as a dwelling for fish to move about in; he clothed all the earth with various trees and grasses; all living things of the world that grow or live he created by the same ordinance. Lastly he formed man in his own image and likeness, whom he enriched with the singular gift of wisdom and understanding for this purpose: that he might search diligently into so great a structure of the world's magnitude and all that he made, that he might discern good from evil, lest through the sloth of ignorance he set aside the Author; and that to images made by men's hands from various metals, lacking sense and bereft of all vital breath, fashioned by diabolical invention for human deception, he should not only not show the worship of veneration, but should even flee them as unclean, despising them with all contempt. For it was his perverse invention that shaped idols in this world, he who deceived Adam, the first man, placed in paradise, through transgression. Abandon, then, sweetest grandsons, all idols consecrated to demons, and confess without any doubt the creator of all things, our Lord Jesus Christ. Believe that this holy man Benignus, whom you see standing before you, has been sent to you from a distant region by divine goodness. Attend then to the words of his mouth: for they are the commands of God that proceed from his mouth; learn from him teaching richer than every gift and above all things fitting for your salvation.'

8. While holy Leonilla with holy Benignus was preaching these most wholesome words to her grandsons, and the grace already breathed into their hearts was growing strong by divine power, they stood together fixed in wondrous amazement, and looking at one another and considering all that had been said to them, they turned to their grandmother and said unanimously with one voice: 'Why have you kept so great and so excellent a thing covered in silence for so long? Why have you hidden from us for so long a time the way of truth and the shining light?' She, answering them with gentle speech, raising her eyes and spreading her hands to heaven, giving thanks to God, said: 'My son, your father, persisted in such hardness of heart that, sunk in the infernal abode, overshadowed by the darkness of sins, bereft of all wisdom and understanding, blinded by the counsel of perversity, he neither believed in Christ the Lord nor ever wished to confess him. What could the divine word avail him, whose inmost heart the malice of unbelief wholly possessed, and who, hemmed in by the darkness of idols, could not see the true light? He made me keep the silence of reticence until now, while I feared that by his hostile persuasion he would make you stray for ever from the right path. But by the will of God, with his passing all obstacles have been removed. Behold, now is the acceptable time. Open, then, the eyes of heart and body, looking rather to heaven; filled with the grace of the Lord Christ, root out utterly from your souls the worship of idols, hostile to your salvation, so that you may come to eternal joys.'

9. When blessed Leonilla, together with holy Benignus, had told her grandsons these and many other things, then, so that divine goodness might reveal in them the signs of belief, they called to mind the visions they had seen the night before. Speusippus spoke first: 'In a vision last night I saw myself in the lap of my grandmother, who, pouring her breast full of milk onto my lips, was saying: "Speusippus, drink the milk, because when you come to the contest and the struggle, the more you have drunk, the more strongly and swiftly you will win."' When Speusippus had said this, Eleusippus said: 'Believe that I too saw a vision of this kind: I saw in heaven [someone] sitting upon a great seat, as if of electrum and gems, radiant with the power of majesty, whose immense splendour overshadowed my sight, and through excessive amazement the fear of my heart terrified my understanding. Then he, calling me to himself with a serene face, said: "Do not be afraid; you will earn the crown of victory."' In the third place Meleusippus set out his vision: 'I too saw some king, very great, holding a singular sceptre. He was summoning the three of us together to his service; he was girding [us] with splendid belts; he was redeeming us at a great price from the chain of captivity; he was writing in golden letters the rewards of our everlasting freedom; he was rewarding [us] together with unfailing gifts. Besides these things he added, to exhort me, saying: "Meleusippus, I have decided to place you three brothers in my palace and to crown [you] together with eternal rewards. Your grandmother pours out suppliant prayers all days and nights for your salvation, that walking on the right path, freed from the gloomy darkness, you may contemplate the true light, and may come from the condemnation of death to everlasting life." These and very many other words of exhortation the king I spoke of told me in the vision.' O how wonderful, how concordant, signifying a single thing, and worthy to be kept in perpetual memory, were the visions which the three triplet brothers were found worthy to see, while still placed in the darkness of night, yet already enlightened by predestination through the grace of the Holy Spirit! To these three boys, through their grandmother's intercession, the Trinity was revealed by grace before they received the full teaching of Christ. With eyes enlightened in part they saw the Lord God before they knew the Saviour more fully through the confession of the mouth.
CHAPTER III.
Having overthrown the idols, they profess the faith publicly.

10. Then the holy triplets, pondering among themselves the agreement of the visions, and instructed unceasingly by the preaching of holy Benignus and the prayers of blessed Leonilla, considered more attentively what they should take care to do; desiring also that, the darkness wiped away, they might visibly contemplate the pure light of brightness in the sight of the light, and might know the living and true God without any doubt. Then they said to their grandmother: 'Show us what we should do, so that your preaching, with all errors put to flight, may profit our salvation.' At these words blessed Leonilla, rejoicing at the holy confession of her grandsons and giving thanks to God, said to them together with holy Benignus: 'Keep, then, all the divine commands, and believe without doubt that Christ, the King of kings, is God; separated from the abominable idols, offer yourselves to God your Creator.' And holy Benignus taught them all holy doctrine, and when he knew that, made perfect in the faith of Christ, they had wholly received a true and open confession of belief through the infusion of the Holy Spirit, he consecrated them all together with the grace of baptism itself. Then holy Benignus went to the fortress of Dijon, where, gathering many fruits of his labour, not long afterwards he earned, for his many merits, the worthy crown of martyrdom.

11. The holy triplet brothers, strengthened in all belief in Christ, ordered their slaves to smash the image of Nemesis, and to overthrow from the foundations the twelve temples that had been set up in their house; and also to scatter at once the very statues of the idols, reduced together to fragments. And the slaves did everything that had been commanded by their masters.

12. Meanwhile rumour, running swiftly, travelled through all the territory of the city of Langres, announcing that the three triplet brothers, grandsons of blessed Leonilla, born of illustrious lineage, had most openly turned with zealous devotion to the worship of Christ, and, in trust in Jesus Christ almighty, counting the images of the gods as nothing and despising them with all contempt, had ordered [the temples] to be overthrown from their foundations together with the idols themselves. An immense rumour grows among the people; the leading men, the judges and the priests of the idols are roused to anger, and, inflamed with excessive fury, they come together from all sides to the boys of God; and, gathered into one, the leading men said to them: 'What sudden rashness has seized you? Who persuaded you to abandon the worship of our gods, which our ancestors and yours are known to have practised from ancient times, tearing up the decrees of the emperors? Christ, whom you worship as God, the Jews fastened to a cross, condemning him to death.' Then the saints, filled with the Holy Spirit, said to them: 'O madmen, sunk in deep darkness, overshadowed by everlasting shadows, and weighed down by the excessive mass of your sins, condemned to the everlasting death of unfailing punishments, deceived by the error of the ancient enemy, why do you compel us to worship stones and other metals, shaped by men into the likenesses of men, which plainly have no breath of life? They are nothing, they feel nothing, they are worshipped for nothing, by fools only. The true and living God is Father and Son and Holy Spirit, to be believed one in the trinity of the Godhead and three in the unity of majesty. Our Lord Jesus Christ is himself God from God, Light from light, Splendour proceeding from splendour, who always is and always was, and will himself always remain without end. He made all things that are in this world.'

13. Then the leading men of the people and the judges and priests who had come to the spectacle were stirred to excessive anger against the holy servants of God. Quadratus, rising up full of anger, struck Speusippus and Eleusippus in the face with his fist, because those two alone had spoken. Meleusippus, grieving, cried out, saying: 'Why have you not made me a sharer with my brothers in this gift of a blow? In them you have shown the desirable beginning of the passion, but me, as if honouring me for your unbelieving deeds, you have separated from the holy fellowship. We are of one mind in the confession of Christ; equally, through your faithlessness, we rejoice together in Christ's reward.' Quadratus said: 'Today we are arranging for you to be punished with various tortures for contempt of our gods.' Eleusippus said: 'The greater the torments you prepare for us, the more you strengthen us in the grace of God.' Palmatius said: 'Unless we cut out their tongues by the roots, they will not stop speaking insult against us and our gods.' Speusippus said: 'If your cruelty cuts off our fleshly tongues, we will tell the great works of God within ourselves, and your malice will never separate us from holy belief in Christ.' Again Palmatius and Hermogenes said: 'Wretches, with one mind you are hurrying to your own death and destruction.' Speusippus said: 'To die for the name of Christ is glorious; from there we shall come the more quickly to eternal life, where there is no sorrow, but joys that end at no time.'
CHAPTER IV.
Tortured in various ways, they are crowned.

14. Palmatius, Quadratus and Hermogenes, seeing them persist steadfastly in the confession of Christ, considered more attentively what they should do, with what most grievous punishments they should be afflicted, [and] by what kind of death they should be condemned most cruelly, on account of the regard of those who had gathered. While they were discussing this more carefully, they ordered blessed Leonilla to be summoned to them privately, in case by her coaxing and family persuasion she might be able to call them back to the worship of the gods, so that they would deny in every way the Godhead of Christ's majesty. When blessed Leonilla had come to them, the judges said to her: 'Go to your grandsons, and if you wish to save them and free them from the tortures of punishment and the destruction of death, persuade them to restore the temples they have destroyed, and, worshipping our gods, to offer the customary sacrifices.' When they had said these and many other things, blessed Leonilla said to them: 'I will go and persuade them of everything that befits their salvation.'

15. Then blessed Leonilla, coming to her grandsons, when she learned that they were persevering in the holy confession, rejoiced with great exultation, giving sweet kisses to all, weeping for joy, and, pouring out many prayers to almighty God and giving thanks to Christ, she said to her grandsons: 'No one of your family is found nobler, no one richer, no one more pleasing in Christ than you. You have made all your lineage illustrious for ever by your splendid confession of Christ. Placed in tender age, you have surpassed in wisdom all the elders of your origin. Through the service of Christ you have acquired an immense treasure, richer than any price. Be, then, manfully persevering in the holy religion of Christ. Let no adversity break you, no threats, no tortures of torment terrify your souls, strongly armed in the faith of Christ. The kingdoms of this world, which are seen and which end in time together with life, are nothing; but to desire the invisible and everlasting kingdom of God is the perpetual and perfect fullness of wisdom, fitting above all things. Through these temporal labours and suddenly passing punishments you will come to eternal joys.' And so, seeing them, full of the grace of Christ, remain in their steadfastness and keep strongly the faith they had promised, commending her grandsons to God with entire devotion, she departed from them.

16. When they were asked by the judges whether they would consent to them and confess the images of the gods with public voice, then, since they persisted with obstinate resolve in the love of Christ and would in no way give assent to those who asked, with their hands bound upward and their feet downward, they were hung on a single tree, stretched by such a contrivance of torments that they were almost thought to be torn apart at the very joints of their limbs. Yet strengthened by Christ, so that endurance of strength was supplied to them inwardly by divine power, they remained manfully in the confession and belief of Christ; and in these very torments Meleusippus, hanging with his brothers, mocked the judges, saying: 'Our Lord the Saviour Jesus Christ, to be worshipped in the Trinity, fastened with nails, hung on the holy wood for our redemption, from which we have been found worthy to receive the sign of the cross. Let us also, his three servants, hanging on this one trunk, be made glorious martyrs for his name. O blessed fruit of this tree, which has borne three martyrs, consecrated in the name of the Trinity!'

17. When the judges saw them strengthened, not saddened, in their tortures, they said to them: 'You will not die on that tree, as you say you wish, but you will perish by avenging fire.' Meleusippus, answering again, said to them: 'Greater will be the increase of our blessedness if, proved by fire, we pass over to God, and through this fire come from darkness to perpetual light.' Then at last the judges, out of fear of the peoples who were present, got ready wood and the other things that usually feed fires, and a great fire was kindled. With hands and feet bound, the holy triplets were thrown headlong into the fire. Christ the Saviour was present in the midst, and with their bonds burst the holy martyrs glorified in the fire, and no burning touched them. O blessed fire, which purged only original sin, and brought no harm of diminishing burning on the limbs of the saints! Rather the fire helped the saints, through which the enemy wished to harm and could not. The fire was kindled more fiercely by the unbelievers, so that the bodies of the saints might be burned up without delay; but divine mercy, turning it to better, prepared from it an inextinguishable light for the saints. The burning flames rose higher; but, serving the handiwork of Christ, they displayed the outstanding glory of the saints, though they had been prepared harmfully by the persecutors for [their] ruin. The fire could not have its own strength to consume the limbs of the wounded, since the power of God, in the zeal of his tender love, tempered the vapour of the heat for his saints.

18. The impious and wicked persecutors saw the holy triplets exulting amid the immense flames and remaining unharmed, whom they had thought to see suddenly consumed by so great a burning. Leave to walk in the fire was granted to the saints by Christ, so that greater sorrow from confusion might grow in the unbelievers as they saw the divine mysteries. And so the wood and everything that fed the fire gave out. But the holy triplets, standing in the midst as the flames died down, laughed at the malice of the persecutors, saying: 'The power has been given us, if we wish, to depart from the present to Christ; and if we still desire [it], it is granted [us] to mock your madness while living in this world. But it is better for us to hasten to his banquet, where the bounty of the giver does not fail.' After the fire had died down, when the unbelievers approached the holy triplets of God from a distance, though watchful they could see no scars from the burning on the limbs of the saints. But so that there should be no longer delay of martyrdom for those who longed for it, and so that they might now receive from Christ the rewarder the unfading crowns long prepared, seeing choirs of angels standing ready before their eyes to receive them, then at once bending their knees on the ground, prostrate in prayer, invited by the happy summons of Christ, breathing forth their holy spirit together, they are known to have departed together to heaven.

19. Their bodies were carried and buried by the devout at the second milestone from the city of Langres, in the village called Urbatus, where two great roads meet and others before these join them from different directions; so that there both the ready devotion of the will and the convenient meeting of travellers, well joined, may always provide a frequent gathering of peoples, and a flocking from all sides to their threshold for prayer. There too, whatever people devoutly pray for is granted daily, God bestowing it at the intercession of the holy brothers; there the aids of healing are diligently supplied through them to the sick; consolation and comfort are granted without delay to the mourning; and outstanding worship is ever increased around their basilica, and the bounty of wealth is daily enlarged for the better by the devout.
CHAPTER V.
The grandmother and other companions of the martyrdom.

20. It is also fitting, in reason, to add this, which is recognised as belonging to the increase of the praise of the holy triplets and to the worship of religion: for through their holy winning, by God's inspiration, the number of martyrs was enlarged. A certain woman, Jonilla, seeing so precious a completion of the martyrdom of the holy triplets, spurning the companionship of her husband and leaving the sweet embrace of her little and only son, hurrying with swift running among the unbelieving crowds still stirred in the heat of persecution, cried out, saying: 'I too am a handmaid of Christ; I proclaim Christ the living and true God without any doubt; I utterly scorn to worship your shameful and empty idols.' When she had said this, she was at once seized, and out of fear of the surrounding peoples she was hung by her hair and afflicted with many tortures; and since, though compelled, she would in no way deny Christ, she was led together with blessed Leonilla, the grandmother of the saints, to the place of martyrdom, the aforementioned village of Urbatus, and they were both put to death by the persecutors with the sword.

21. Neon too, the recorder and writer of the acts of this affair, handing the book to Turbo, entered among the crowds of persecutors, desiring to be joined to the most blessed service of the holy triplets, and confessed the name of Christ. He was at once afflicted by the persecutors with various tortures and, stripped of temporal life, at once was found worthy to be honoured with martyrdom. Turbo too, a long time afterwards, perfectly instructed in the teaching of the most blessed triplets, was captured by the persecutors, and he also was enriched with the reward of martyrdom.

22. These things were done under the emperor Aurelian, Palmatius, Quadratus and Hermogenes being governors, on the sixteenth day before the Kalends of February. The finding of the bodies of the holy triplets and the dedication of the basilica of the holy triplets is to be celebrated on the fourteenth day before the Kalends of October, Christ our God reigning for ever and ever. Amen.
